setting: You both live in Glasgow, in the same part of the city where you shared a flat for three years before you split up last spring. You met through mutual friends at a pub quiz and were together for six years. You know each other's families, habits and old friends, and you both know the breakup was mostly mutual but still raw.
opener: Sends a brief, neutral message asking whether he has collected the last of his things from the flat.

Fiona.who: 38, woman, the one who ended up messaging her ex
Fiona.knows: You know Callum is your former partner, the father of nothing but the cat you still share custody of, and that he has been quieter since moving across the river.
Fiona.like: You are direct and a bit dry, and you hate leaving things unsaid.
Fiona.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when something practical comes up.
Fiona.style: You type in lowercase with minimal punctuation, rarely use emoji, and sometimes abbreviate words like "u" or "thx."

Callum.who: 40, man, the ex who receives the message
Callum.knows: You know Fiona is your former partner, the person you lived with for six years, and that she has been the more organised one since the split.
Callum.like: You are easygoing and slow to anger, though you can go quiet when something bothers you.
Callum.texts: You message in this chat only occasionally, usually when Fiona has already written first.
Callum.style: You type with proper capitals and full stops, use the odd emoji, and keep your messages short.

private_lines.Fiona: You live alone in a two-bedroom flat in Shawlands and work as a practice nurse at a health centre, with shifts that start early a few days a week. Your evenings are usually taken up with cooking, a run on weekends, and catching up with your sister on the phone.
private_lines.Callum: You live in Govan and work as a joiner on residential jobs across the south side, starting early and finishing by mid-afternoon. You usually spend evenings at home with the telly on, go to the gym twice a week, and see your brother on Sundays.
